The source is a far-sided high southern latitude filament eruption observed in GOES SUVI 304 over the S limb at 2026-06-11T19:32Z and on/beyond the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-06-11T20:15Z.

data.note: Narrow CME seen to the southeast in STEREO A COR2A and very dimly to the due south in SOHO LASCO C2 which is likely associated with an eruption with dimming from AR 14464 near S12W20 around 2026-06-12T13:50Z seen best in SDO AIA composite imagery using the sum of 211/193/171 Angstrom imagers. Also seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

data.note: Faint partial halo CME seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 directed towards the east. The CME narrower with a brighter bulk and disconnected bulk/shock as seen in STEREO A COR2A, with a brighter bulk to the east-northeast and shock extending from the southeast to the north. This CME is associated with a filament eruption near N00E35 erupting near 2026-06-12T16:15Z, best seen in SDO AIA composite imagery using the sum of 211/193/171 Angstroms and as well in GOES SUVI/SDO AIA 304 Angstroms. This CME, seen due east and northeast in COR2A, is seen overlapping the previous CME: 2026-06-12T15:38Z which is seen to the southeast and which is a separate eruption.

The source of this event is a filament eruption likely originating from the far side seen in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-06-12T18:16Z. Faint field line movement can also be seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 in association with this eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

The source of this event is a filament eruption seen along the Eastern limb (approx. S10E80 with some Northern deflection) in SDO AIA /GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-06-12T18:56Z. Wide opening field lines and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

The source of this event is likely continued outflow following a large filament eruption resulting in CME: 2026-06-12T19:24Z.

This CME is most likely far-sided as no source candidate was found on the Earth-facing disk. This is consistent with the triangulated measurement.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 stating at 2026-06-13T13:26Z. It is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the S in STEREO A COR2. The majority of this CME was missed by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time due to a data gap between downlink periods. The source of this CME is a large eruption in across the far SE portion of the Earth-facing disk centered around AR 14461 (S21W68). The eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 193 as wide opening field lines accompanied by dimming and an EUVI wave beginning around 2026-06-13T12:36Z. This CME is also associated with a C2.5 class flare from AR 14461 which peaked at 2026-06-13T13:09Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen because this feature is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and does not have a source candidate on the Earth-facing disk.

The source of this event is a large, slow prominence eruption beginning at approx. 2026-06-15T03:00Z, with liftoff beginning at 2026-06-15T06:00Z as seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. The source of this event is faint field line opening seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA beginning at approx. 2026-06-15T07:00Z. This CME heavily overlaps with CME: 2026-06-15T06:36Z which is related to a large prominence eruption.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery and can be seen faintly and partially obscured by the pylon GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is far-sided and is likely related to a filament eruption originating from beyond the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-06-16T18:45Z. Faint field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery around this time.

The source is an eruption from Active Region 14464 (~S14W90) starting around 2026-06-17T12:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery.

data.note: CME first seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-17T17:48Z. It is also seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This is the first in a series of three CMEs. The source is an eruption from Active Region 14464 (~S14W96) starting around 2026-06-17T17:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

data.note: CME first seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-17T18:48Z. It is also seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2, likely because it is obscured by the occulting disk. This is the second in a series of three CMEs and over takes the first CME: 2026-06-17T18:00Z. The source of this CME is a small filament eruption over the NW limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 starting as early as 2026-06-17T18:33Z. A small eruption can be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 from the vicinity of former Active Region 14463 (~N17W93) beginning around 2026-06-17T18:35Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-17T20:24Z. It is also seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2, likely because it is obscured by the occulting disk. This is the third in a series of three CMEs. The source of this CME is most likely a small eruption from beyond the W limb from the vicinity of former AR 14464. Ejecta can be seen in SDO AIA 304 starting around 2026-06-17T19:48Z, and the eruption can be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning around 2026-06-17T19:55Z.

The source of this CME is most likely a small filament eruption from beyond the NW limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-06-17T23:24Z, likely from former AR 14463 (N17W96).

This CME quickly overtakes CME: 2026-06-18T01:28Z likely from the same source, former AR 14464 over the SW limb ~S14W100, observed in GOES SUVI 171 as field line movement over the SW limb starting around 2026-06-18T01:56Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only analysis using W100 as the approximate location of former AR 14464, as such the longitude could vary slightly if the eruption is further deflected. The front may be faintly visible in STEREO A COR2, but is difficult to resolve and triangulate with if so.

data.note: CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and faintly to the W in STEREO A COR, as the CME was directed more directly towards STEREO A. The source is far-sided, and a complex eruption between two active regions, AR 14463 (N17W97) and AR 14464 (S14W100). Starting around 2026-06-18T05:36Z, filament ejecta is observed in SDO AIA 304 erupting from AR 14463, deflecting southward towards AR 14464 which triggers a larger filament ejecta and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/304 starting around 2026-06-18T06:09Z (as such, is considered the main source of material). This is also observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-06-18T05:45Z, and as an area of weak dimming between the regions centered ~N00W90.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the faint front perspective in STEREO A COR makes it difficult to resolve in imagery. Triangulates well deflected to ~W80 from the observed source ~W100.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 and S in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1. No distinct source for this CME is observed but triangulates ~W171 on the far-side from Earth. It might be seen as field line movement on the SW limb of STEREO A EUVI 195 starting at 2026-06-18T07:05Z, but the signature is so weak that this could be EUVI image artefacting.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed only in SOHO LASCO C2 to the far high-latitude North. Source is likely a filament ejecta and field line movement over the N limb, observed in GOES SUVI 284/304 starting around 2026-06-18T11:16Z. CME front is faint and fades into background after several C2 frames.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 plane-of-sky. CME front is faint and fades into background after several C2 frames.

data.note: CME observed to the SW only in STEREO A COR2. Two close fronts appear identical and traveling together at 2026-06-18T13:23Z and 2026-06-18T13:53Z; as such without a second source eruption this CME entry serves as tracking both together with the leading-most edge 2026-06-18T13:23Z. The source is likely a filament eruption from former AR 14466 on the far-side from Earth, located around N05W140 at this time, observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 starting at 2026-06-18T11:45Z as the filament brightening and then disappearing.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only analysis of the leading-most edge, using W140 as the approximate longitude of the source observed near STEREO A's west limb. The parameters, particularly longitude, could easily vary within a few degrees with any deflection of the eruption.

data.note: CME visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The start of the CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2026-06-18T19:38Z to 2026-06-19T00:38Z. The source is a filament eruption best seen off the west limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting at 2026-06-18T23:37Z. Opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: Faint CME visible to the SE in STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around S40E40 as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery with liftoff starting around 2026-06-18T21:36Z. Dimming is also seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery. The eruption is not visible in STEREO A EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location. The CME is faint and only measurable in four frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1, likely due to the CME's faintness. The candidate source eruption can be seen near the southwest limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2026-06-19T05:55Z as opening field lines.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as potential source location.

data.note: CME faintly visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is an eruption with dimming seen in SDO AIA 193 centered at N10E55 starting around 2026-06-19T13:36Z. Moving field lines are also seen off the east limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery and may correspond to this eruption. A small eruption from AR 14470 (N07E32) was also seen around the same time, but the eruption around N10E55 was determined to be the most likely source candidate.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the west in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is an eruption seen around S10W130 in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery starting at 2026-06-20T00:45Z, directly following a data gap from 2026-06-19T19:15Z to 2026-06-20T00:45Z. The eruption is also seen beyond the west limb in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 284/304 starting around 2026-06-20T00:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location.

data.note: CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an M1.3 flare from AR 14472 (S12E70) peaking at 2026-06-20T01:51Z. An eruption with dimming and opening field lines is best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-2 and the north in STEREO A COR2. The source is an eruption beyond the NE limb as seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting at 2026-06-20T02:49Z. Moving field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source seen in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: Faint CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2. The CME is not clearly visible in other coronagraph imagery, and the leading edge is faint. The potential source may be a region of dimming seen around N00W45 starting around 2026-06-20T11:00Z in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location using SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery.

data.note: Very faint, narrow CME first seen to the NNE part way into the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-20T20:00Z. It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3 and briefly in GOES CCOR-1. It is not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source candidate was found for this CME on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Very faint, wide CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 only. The CME disappears half-way through the C2 field of view. The potential source for this CME is the M2.6 flare peaking at 2026-06-21T02:46Z from Active Region 14473 (S08E67) as seen in SDO/AIA 131. There is an associated failed filament eruption in SDO/AIA 304 starting around 2026-06-21T2:39Z through 2026-06-21T03:30Z. Additionally, there are moving/opening field lines visible in SDO/AIA 131 starting around 2026-06-21T02:55Z which appear to be successful in releasing from the lower corona.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on source location and best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Due to this, some uncertainty with parameters is present.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the W in STEREO A COR2 imagery. It may be faintly visible to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 for a frame, but it is hard to tell for sure. The source of this CME appears to be filament ejecta from along the Western limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-06-21T07:15Z, possibly associated with old Active Regions 14464 and 14467 beyond the SW limb from STEREO A's point of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 imagery and using SOHO LASCO C2's view of the possible associated front. Higher degree of uncertainty due to limited viewpoints.

data.note: This CME is visible to the W/SW in STEREO A COR2 and to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source of this CME may be from activity beyond the W/SW limb as seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery, possibly associated with old Active Regions 14464 and 14467 beyond the SW limb from STEREO A's point of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the W in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be associated with eruption activity from beyond the W/SW limb, possibly associated with old ARs 14464/14467 starting around 2026-06-21T10:15Z in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on potential source location with variability in longitude likely (+/- 10 to 15 degrees) due to limited viewpoints.

data.note: This CME is visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be associated with eruption activity from beyond the W/SW limb, possibly associated with old Active Regions 14464 and 14467.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a far-sided eruption visible near the western limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-06-21T16:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the approximate source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a far-sided eruption visible near the western limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-06-21T18:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source longitude.

data.note: This CME is visible to the east/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2026-06-21T19:53Z. The source is an M6.8 flare from Active Region 14473 (S09E57) starting around 2026-06-21T19:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. An EUV wave is observed surrounding the eruption site in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195 at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the Northeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-21T23:00Z. This CME is not clearly seen in other coronagraphs. The source is a far-sided eruption visible over the northeast limb starting around 2026-06-21T21:33Z seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of E90 due to source from beyond the NE limb and lack of coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: Narrow and faint CME visible to the West in STEREO A COR2 imagery and faintly visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 difference imagery. The source of this CME is not clearly seen due to a data gap prior to the CME start time, but may possibly be associated with eruption activity from the area of old Active Regions 14464 and 14467 beyond the W/SW limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. This CME is possibly associated with a small filament eruption starting around 2026-06-22T00:00Z from an unnumbered region near N07E32. This location is in close proximity to an equatorial coronal hole to the West of the source region, and the CME may be deflected to the east as a result.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: This CME is visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 imagery and faintly to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source of this CME appears to be filament ejecta from farsided eruption activity possibly associated with old Active Regions 14464 and 14467.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 imagery and faintly to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source of this CME appears to be filament ejecta from farsided eruption activity possibly associated with old Active Regions 14464 and 14467. This CME overlaps the CME first seen to the SW in STEREO A COR2 imagery at 2026-06-22T03:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.

data.note: Faint CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 due to being far sided from the STEREO A perspective. The source of this CME is a filament eruption visible to the E in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2026-06-22T06:17Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of E90 due to source near the limb and lack of visible STEREO A imagery to triangulate.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the WSW only in STEREO A COR2, likely due to the faint front and being blocked by the SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 occulting disks. The source is unclear but likely far-sided, only potentially seen as a brightening prominence on the west limb in STEREO A COR2 EUVI 304 at 2026-06-22T07:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 plane-of-sky taken atm W151.9 with STEREO A at W61.942. This analysis encompasses the wider of two fronts that appear at this same time, blending together after the first two frames and becoming indistinguishable.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery for a few frames before the leading edge becomes too diffuse to observe. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source for this event is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth or STEREO A-facing disk around the time of this event. A very faint opening of field lines may be visible beyond the southwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery starting around 2026-06-23T08:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 152 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth or STEREO A-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 152 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: Loop CME seen to the east-northeast in SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and STEREO A COR2A. The CME appears to be associated with eruptive activity over the eastern limb, as evidenced by opening field lines bending from eastward to the northeast seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2026-06-23T18:00Z. The full extent of the eruption is better visualized in GOES SUVI 284 imagery, where a faint loop seen stretching from northeast to southeast begins erupting outward off the eastern limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Fairly speculative leading edge measurement using only Sun-Earth line coronagraphs which include SOHO and GOES with no STEREO Ahead imagery, therefore, there is high uncertainty in source longitude by up to 15 degrees.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-23T01:26Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is mostly blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is a region of dimming seen centered at approx. N40E50 beginning at approx. 2026-06-24T00:49Z as seen in SDO AIA 193 with some likely deflection towards the Northwest.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-06-24T13:00Z. This CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink data gap from 2026-06-24T06:24Z to 2026-06-24T15:36Z, and is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to it being far sided from the COR2A perspective. The source of this event is a small eruption from Active Region 14475 (S09E32) beginning at approx. 2026-06-24T10:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint, thin CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, more faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely triggered by AR 14477 (S13E55), with two weak brightenings observed at S11E55 and N00E40 and an area of dimming in between centered around S01E51, all in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-06-25T23:16Z, also observed in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171 as field line movement originating from this area.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Half width is less than 10 degrees in SOHO, appearing slightly more wide in STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and potentially to the SW in STEREO A COR2, it is difficult to resolve but a faint feature is visible in COR2A white light imagery only. No direct source is observed for this event, likely far-sided, and may be visible as weak field line movement in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-06-25T03:31Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky due to the faint front. While a faint signature is observed in STEREO A COR2 white light, it is not resolvable in running difference imagery to reliably triangulate with.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The front starts slow and faint in LASCO C2, becoming more defined further into the respective fields of view. No distinct source is observed for this event, an eruption in SDO AIA 193 from AR 14470 at 2026-06-25T14:37Z was a culprit but occurs too late for the slow start time of this front.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only plane of sky as the CME is blocked by the LASCO C3 pylon.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2, not yet visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink gap and GOES CCOR-1 due to a data gap. The source is a filament eruption over the SW limb from Earth, and on-disk for STEREO A. Observed as filament ejecta over the SW limb in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2026-06-25T13:25Z and also in GOES SUVI 304. Observed on-disk brightening and field line movement in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting at 2026-06-25T13:25Z near former AR 14469, putting the approximate center filament location ~S15W115. Also observed as field line movement and filament ejecta in SDO AIA 131/171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2, and available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery at this time due to a downlink gap.
Preliminary approximation of the far sided source around W115 as viewed in STEREO A EUVI, could vary W105-W125. STEREO A COR2 only observing coronagraph at this time.
